<div class="wrap" markdown="1">

{% raw %}
The Competitive/PvP (FPS & Esports) module is for shooter and esports clans: Counter-Strike 2, Valorant, Overwatch 2, Marvel Rivals, Rainbow Six Siege, Call of Duty, Battlefield and battle royale. Finish [**Setting up Alagos**](/guides/setting-up/) first.

## 1. Switch it on

Run `/guild-settings modules` and press **Switch on** beside **Competitive/PvP (FPS & Esports)**. Alagos calls your group a **Clan**; rename it with **✏️ What we're called** on the Overview tab (to Team or Org, say).

## 2. Players and their games

Members add a character for each game they play from **My profile**: their in-game name, the game, a main and second role (only that game's roles are offered), their rank, and their in-game ID (Riot ID, Steam, Battle.net and so on). Officers can add or fix anyone's.

## 3. Scrims and matches

Press **New event** and pick a template: a scrim for each game (one slot per role, plus substitutes), an official match, a battle royale session or an in-house. Members sign up by role; when a role is full they wait as a substitute and move up by themselves.

After a scrim or match, **🏁 Result** on its post records the opponent and the maps ("Mirage 13-9", your score first). **📊 Our record** shows your wins and losses overall, by game, by map and by opponent. It is also on the game's settings tab.

## 4. Running a league or cup

On the **Features & limits** tab press **🏆 Championships**, then **➕ New championship**: a name, the game, and **Matches** (teams play each other). In the championship:

- **✏️ Settings**: best of 1, 3 or 5, and how long before a reported result counts by itself (24 hours by default).
- **👥 Teams**: each team's name, tag and players, the captain first.
- **🗓️ Fixtures**: make the fixture list (every team plays every other, once or home and away), or add matches yourself.
- **⚖️ Disputes**: the channel where disputed results go to your stewards.
- **📌 Post the standings**: the table, the week's matches, and the captains' buttons.

**🏆 Playoffs** adds a knockout bracket after the league, or makes a cup on its own; a championship of **Rounds** with three to six games is a battle royale series. In-house games are made from the in-house template's post. See [**Running a league of teams**](/guides/fps-running/).

The free plan runs one championship at a time. Your own points and tie-breaks are Premium; the default is 3 for a win, 1 for a draw, 0 for a loss.

## 5. Maps

Counter-Strike 2 and Valorant come with their current map pools. Add the rest, or a new season's maps, in **📚 Game lists** on the game's settings tab.
